interface.title: Peptide Fragmenter
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis and interpretation: checking which theoretical fragment ions of a candidate peptide appear in an MS/MS spectrum
interface.what_it_is_for: Calculate the theoretical a/b/c/x/y/z fragment ions of a modified peptide over a range of charges, then match them to a pasted MS/MS peak list within a Th or ppm tolerance, with an annotated spectrum, a sequence coverage table, Hyperscore/Binomial scores and CSV export.

data.note: The default peptide [164.0700]FDSFGDLSSASAIM(16)GNPK is pre-filled in the sidebar. The Spectra textarea is pre-filled from the repo's samplespectra.txt (15420 characters of m/z–intensity pairs). I also typed a 6-peak spectrum myself and a second peptide, [-3.14]PEP(123.456)TIDE. There is no upload widget, so no test file was uploaded.

tree.general: Find out which theoretical fragments of a candidate molecule explain a measured fragmentation spectrum, and how well they do
tree.specific: Fragment a peptide in silico and annotate/score an MS/MS spectrum against its a/b/c/x/y/z ions

features.name: Modified-sequence input
features.general: A text field for a sequence written with inline mass modifications on residues and termini, which drives every downstream calculation
features.specific: Sidebar Peptide Sequence: (mass) after a residue for residue mods, [mass] at the start for N-terminal mods; press Enter to recompute. A parenthesised N-terminal mod, as in the Help example (-3.14)PEP(123.456)TIDE, crashes with KeyError '-'
steps: add residue mods as (mass) after the residue
add an N-terminal mod as [mass] at the start
press Enter and check the recomputed tables
serves_tasks: Enter the molecule, including chemical modifications

features.name: Per-charge fragment ladder tables
features.general: Choose a charge range, a mass model and which cleavage series to include, and get one ladder table per charge state
features.specific: Min/Max Charge, monoisotopic/average and the a/b/c/x/y/z multiselect drive the Charge N tables on the Results tab (AA, #(abc), colour-coded ion columns, #(xyz)). Internal Fragments does not change these tables
steps: set the min and max charge
add or remove ion types in the multiselect
serves_tasks: Set the range of charge states to calculate
Choose which fragment series to calculate
Read the theoretical fragment values per position and charge

features.name: Fragment segment map (mass vs. sequence span)
features.general: Plot every theoretical fragment as a line spanning the part of the sequence it contains, placed at its mass and coloured by series, with hover labels and box zoom
features.specific: Plotly 'Fragment Segments' chart: x = M/Z, y = residues; each ion is a vertical segment over its residues, coloured by ion type; hover shows (m/z, residue) and a label such as +y15 (the pointer must land exactly on the thin segment)
steps: change the sequence or ion types in the sidebar
hover a segment to read its ion label and m/z
drag a box to zoom into an m/z window
serves_tasks: See graphically which part of the molecule each fragment covers, and at what mass

features.name: Pasted peak-list matcher with Th/ppm tolerance and intensity cut-off
features.general: Paste a two-column peak list, set a match tolerance in absolute or relative units and an intensity threshold, and have each peak assigned to the nearest theoretical fragment
features.specific: Spectra tab: the Spectra textarea ('m/z intensity' per line, pre-filled from samplespectra.txt), Tolerance plus Tolerance Type (th | ppm; switching to ppm resets the value to 50) and Min Intensity. Results update on Enter or Ctrl+Enter
steps: paste or edit peaks in the textarea and press Ctrl+Enter
watch the plot, coverage table and scores update
serves_tasks: Set how close a peak must be to count as a match, in absolute or relative units

features.name: Annotated spectrum bar chart with ion-type legend filtering
features.general: Show the measured spectrum as bars with the matched peaks coloured and labelled by assignment; toggle categories from the legend and box-zoom into regions
features.specific: Plotly 'Spectra Plot': unmatched peaks are grey; matched peaks are coloured by ion_color_type (y red, b blue, c green, x orange, internal fragments magenta 'i') and labelled +y11, ++c14, +++y18, +++b18i; click a legend swatch to hide a series (its text labels stay), drag to zoom, double-click to reset
steps: click a legend swatch to hide or show an ion series
drag a box to zoom into an m/z range
serves_tasks: See which peaks were explained and by which fragment

features.name: Sequence coverage table with matched-cell highlighting
features.general: A residue-by-series grid of theoretical values in which the cells supported by a measured peak are highlighted, showing at a glance which cleavage sites are covered
features.specific: Under the scores: rows are residues, columns are ion type × charge (b1, b2, b3, c1 … y3). Matched cells are yellow; cells matched only by internal fragments are magenta. CAVEAT: x/y/z highlights land on the mirrored row because highlight_cells uses row+1 for every series while C-terminal columns are reversed (app.py:337); trust only a/b/c highlights
steps: read the highlighted cells by residue and series
change tolerance or intensity and compare the coverage
serves_tasks: See which positions in the sequence have supporting evidence

features.name: Match-quality score readout
features.general: Summarise a spectrum-to-candidate match as two numbers that can be compared across settings or candidates
features.specific: Hyperscore and Binomial Score metrics, shown with the caveat 'Score are under development and may not be accurate'
serves_tasks: Get summary scores for how well the spectrum matches the candidate, re-reading them after changing settings
Compare alternative candidates against the same spectrum

features.name: Expandable data table with CSV export
features.general: Collapse the full long-format result table under an expander with a data grid and a one-click CSV download
features.specific: 'Fragment Ion Data' (fragment_ions.csv) on Results and 'Spectra Data' (spectra_results.csv) on Spectra, each with a dataframe grid and a Download CSV button
serves_tasks: Export the full fragment list for downstream analysis
